prompt_text: Write exactly 150 words in second-person perspective describing the experience of waking up as the first uploaded consciousness. You may not use the words 'time' or 'future' explicitly.
response: The recipe was written on the inside of a coffin lid, in a script part chemical notation, part prayer. Chef Mara translated it slowly: Take grief, two cups, reduced over low flame until syrupy. Fold in one unspoken apology, beaten to stiff peaks. Bake at the temperature of the last conversation you had with her. The kitchen filled with a smell like rain on hot asphalt. When the timer rang, Mara opened the oven. On the rack sat not a cake but a door, small as a breadbox, made of glazed ceramic and memory. She knocked. From the other side came footsteps, then silence, then a voice: You never brought me dessert. Mara wept, tasting salt and sugar. The recipe had never been about baking. It was about knocking.
